newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks open soft in dismal trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks open soft in dismal trade.

text.p: The Singapore stock market opened on a soft, dismal note on Monday, with crossed trades dominating activities.
Dealers said sentiment was lacklustre, dampened by the 53.38 point drop on Wall Street on Friday and by uncertainty over its near-term direction.
At 0200 GMT, the benchmark Straits times Industrials Index was down 0.64 points at 2,018.96. Turnover was a dull 3.4 million shares with seven losers against three gainers.

Electro Resource, which topped the actives, had 942,000 shares crossed at S$2.729, dealers said. Jardine Matheson saw 765,200 shares crossed at US$5.467 and US$5.492. The shares were down US$0.10 at US$5.30 by 0200 GMT.

About 500,000 shares of Singapore Telecommunications Ltd shares were crossed at S$2.529. The rise of the stock was capped by the price war in Singapore's telecommunications market that erupted when new players entered the market on April 1.

Creative Technology hit a new year high at S$21.80 before slipping to S$21.60, up S$1.30, after the multimedia company posted better than expected net profits of US$44.2 million for third quarter ended March 31, 1997.
